speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly when the bilious vomiting started after birth, and has the baby passed any meconium yet?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby passed any meconium or gas since birth, and is there any visible abdominal distension? Given the family history of pyloric stenosis, I want to clarify if the vomiting was initially non-bilious before turning bilious.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray to evaluate for bowel obstruction and gas patterns. Since the vomiting is bilious and started immediately, I need to rule out intestinal malrotation or atresia rather than pyloric stenosis. Has the baby passed any meconium or gas since birth?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal X-ray shows a 'double bubble' sign indicative of duodenal atresia.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Brother had pyloric stenosis. Social history: NA

speaker: Patient
text: Physical examination shows epicanthus, upward slanting of the eyelids, low-set ears, and a single transverse palmar crease. speaker: Doctor
text:
The physical findings of epicanthus, upward-slanting palpebral fissures, low-set ears, and a single transverse palmar crease are classic signs of Down syndrome, which is strongly associated with duodenal atresia causing bilious vomiting.

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray to look for the "double bubble" sign.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia
